chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (mercy of God be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ahmad ibn Idris said on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of Ali ibn Sayf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn 'Ubaydah, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about the vision [of God] and what the general and special people narrate regarding it, and I asked him to explain it to me. So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting:

All agree, there is no disagreement among them, that knowledge via vision is necessary. So, if it is permissible for Allah, the Mighty and High, to be seen by the eye, then knowledge occurs necessarily. Then that knowledge does not remain except that it is either faith or not faith. If that knowledge via vision is faith, then the knowledge in the abode of this world via acquisition is not faith, because it is its opposite, so no one in this world would be a believer, because they have not seen Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance. And if that knowledge via vision is not faith, then this knowledge which is via acquisition does not remain except that it either vanishes or does not vanish in the Resurrection. This is proof that Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance, is not seen by the eye, because the eye leads to what we described.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia theological argument against seeing God with the physical eye?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) employs a rigorous logical deduction (burhan) to refute the possibility of seeing God with the physical eye, addressing the debate between the general public and scholars. He demonstrates that if visual perception equated to faith, worldly believers would be invalid since they rely on acquired knowledge rather than direct sight; conversely, if it is not faith, then faith would be transient, leading to a contradiction. This hadith is foundational in Shia theology for establishing that divine vision is spiritual/intellectual rather than corporeal, distinguishing it from the vision of Prophet Musa (AS) which was limited to a manifestation of God's light.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub said: Ahmad ibn Idris said on the authority of Ahmad Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of `Ali ibn Sayf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ubaydah that I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (`Ali) al-Rida (AS) asking him about the vision of Allah and what that Sunnis and the Shi`ites narrate regarding the subject. I asked him to explain the subject in detail to me. Hence, he (AS) wrote in his own handwriting:

All agree unanimously that Allah’s recognition is necessary. So, if it is possible to see Allah, the Mighty and High, with the eyes, then recognition has taken place. And this recognition could take place with or without faith. If recognition via vision is faith, then it is not faith, because faith is the opposite of visual recognition. If recognition via vision is faith, then there would be no people of faith in the world since nobody has seen Allah, Exalted is His Remembrance. If faith is based on visual recognition, then it might vanish as a result of death and resurrection. This is sufficient proof that Allah, noble be His Remembrance, cannot be seen by the eye….
